Q: polars full join default null value A:

The join method does not currently have an option for setting a default value for nulls. However, there is an easy way to accomplish this.

Let's say we have this data:

import polars as pl

df1 = pl.DataFrame({"key": ["a", "b", "d"], "var1": [1, 1, 1]})

df2 = pl.DataFrame({"key": ["a", "b", "c"], "var2": [2, 2, 2]})

df1.join(df2, on="key", how="full")

shape: (4, 4)
┌──────┬──────┬───────────┬──────┐
│ key  ┆ var1 ┆ key_right ┆ var2 │
│ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ ---       ┆ ---  │
│ str  ┆ i64  ┆ str       ┆ i64  │
╞══════╪══════╪═══════════╪══════╡
│ a    ┆ 1    ┆ a         ┆ 2    │
│ b    ┆ 1    ┆ b         ┆ 2    │
│ null ┆ null ┆ c         ┆ 2    │
│ d    ┆ 1    ┆ null      ┆ null │
└──────┴──────┴───────────┴──────┘

To create a different value for the null values, simply use this:

df1.join(df2, on="key", how="full").with_columns(pl.exclude("key", "key_right").fill_null(0))

shape: (4, 4)
┌──────┬──────┬───────────┬──────┐
│ key  ┆ var1 ┆ key_right ┆ var2 │
│ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ ---       ┆ ---  │
│ str  ┆ i64  ┆ str       ┆ i64  │
╞══════╪══════╪═══════════╪══════╡
│ a    ┆ 1    ┆ a         ┆ 2    │
│ b    ┆ 1    ┆ b         ┆ 2    │
│ null ┆ 0    ┆ c         ┆ 2    │
│ d    ┆ 1    ┆ null      ┆ 0    │
└──────┴──────┴───────────┴──────┘

Q: Building ndk (ndk-r10b) samples on ubuntu A:

I managed to build https://github.com/android/ndk-samples/commit/988d73bed0fd3dd362d8041a34f958be76769773 on Ubuntu 24.04 + Android Studio 2025.2.3. Each error message was Googleable, but here's a summary:

  • open folder in Android studio
  • click build to download a bunch of stuff you need
  • SDK manager (settings cog on top right > SDK manager)
  • SDK tools
  • Show package details
  • cmake 4.1.0 to overcome: Unable to find CMake in Android Studio
  • Apply

From then on, I have everything I needed to build either from GUI or CLI and obtain all working APKs:

sudo apt install openjdk-17-jdk
JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64 ./gradlew build

I had to downgrade from latest JDK to 17 because the repo currently has Gradle 3.8 and 17 is the newest supported JDK with an Ubuntu package as per: Unable to find CMake in Android Studio

Q: BCrypt vs Argon2 and their hashing algorithms A:

It should be noted that Argon2 is weaker than bcrypt for run times less than 1 second. (i.e. for authentication)

Actually, bcrypt is stronger than Argon2 for authentication (target runtime < 500ms.) Argon2 does not match or surpass bcrypt's strength until >= ~1000ms runtimes (KDF.) So "Use Argon2" is not a good one-size-fits-all answer.

Argon2 is great as as a key derivation function, but the Password Hashing Competition was supposed to be to select one password hashing function to rule them all.

Argon2 isn't bad, it just doesn't fulfill the goal of the PHC; i.e., it doesn't do a better job than existing algorithms for password storage. It's a fantastic KDF, though.

For runtimes of less than 1000ms, Argon2 is weaker than bcrypt.

The Argon2 people focused on "memory-hard" rather than "cache-hard".

Also, bcrypt is stronger than scrypt for memory sizes under 16 MB.

https://blog.ircmaxell.com/2014/03/why-i-dont-recommend-scrypt.html

See Pufferfish2 for a password hashing algorithm that is better than Argon2, scrypt, and bcrypt. It's the bcrypt algorithm extended from a 4 KB buffer, up to a buffer the size of your per-core cache (e.g. 256 KB)
